section_summary: This section begins with 1949 correspondence on Japan’s exchange rate, including SCAP’s detailed case against devaluing the yen after sterling’s devaluation and Washington’s requests for further analysis. It also covers Japan’s budget and stabilization program, counterpart fund loans, precious metal stocks, public employee bonuses, and the status of Japanese dollar bonds. The later pages are largely 1945 letters from bondholders and their representatives, together with State Department replies and internal handling papers.

subfiles.title: Letter on revisions to the Ikeda letter
subfiles.about: The writer describes revisions to a draft letter concerning Japanese taxation and productivity.
subfiles.summary: The writer incorporates State, Treasury, and Army comments, discusses a British taxation comparison, and lists further additions to the Ikeda letter.

subfiles.title: SCAP message on yen–sterling rate adjustment
subfiles.about: SCAP reports instructions to change the yen’s rate against sterling.
subfiles.summary: Japan is instructed to adjust the yen–pound rate from 1,450.8 to 1,008 yen.

subfiles.title: Butterworth memorandum on devaluing the yen
subfiles.about: Butterworth urges prompt consideration of yen devaluation after sterling’s devaluation.
subfiles.summary: He recounts discussions with Voorhees and asks that the rate receive immediate interagency consideration.

subfiles.title: Army request for SCAP’s devaluation analysis
subfiles.about: Washington asks SCAP to assess the effects of currency devaluations on Japanese trade.
subfiles.summary: The Army seeks trade, payments, and commodity information before Dodge’s Washington meetings.

subfiles.title: SCAP analysis opposing yen–dollar devaluation
subfiles.about: SCAP evaluates yen devaluation and concludes the 360-yen dollar rate should remain.
subfiles.summary: The message compares subsidy, budget, export, and trade outcomes under devaluation and no change in the rate. It argues that devaluation would weaken economic stabilization, raise import costs, and reduce pressure for industrial efficiency, while cheaper imports from devalued areas would benefit Japan. It also discusses sterling balances and Commonwealth trade negotiations. SCAP and a separate group of advisers conclude that changing the yen–dollar rate is unwise.

subfiles.title: Army follow-up questions on yen devaluation
subfiles.about: Washington asks SCAP for further evidence on trade effects and timing of yen devaluation.
subfiles.summary: Following talks with Dodge, the Army requests details on sterling-area prices and quantities, export industries, subsidies, aid requirements, and the effect of any delay. It also asks whether sterling balances can be converted at the former dollar rate.

subfiles.title: Memorandum forwarding draft reply on yen devaluation
subfiles.about: A State Department officer forwards a cleared draft reply to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: The memo says Washington agencies presently favor prompt yen devaluation and seek clarification from SCAP.

subfiles.title: Draft reply to SCAP on devaluation
subfiles.about: A draft asks detailed questions about yen devaluation and Japanese trade.
subfiles.summary: The draft closely parallels the Army’s September 30 message. It questions SCAP about export competitiveness, sterling-area trade, the budget, aid, timing, and convertibility of sterling balances.

subfiles.title: Questions for SCAP on sterling devaluation’s effect on Japan
subfiles.from: Office of Financial and Development Policy
subfiles.about: A proposed set of questions examines the effects of sterling devaluation on Japan.
subfiles.summary: The questions cover trade commitments, textiles, export industries, subsidies, aid, sterling balances, and the timing of any yen adjustment.

subfiles.title: Routing note on Japanese securities
subfiles.about: A damaged note introduces correspondence on Japanese foreign-currency securities.
subfiles.summary: The surviving text refers to securities and an accompanying radio message.

subfiles.title: Draft message on foreign-currency securities
subfiles.about: A badly damaged draft discusses Japanese foreign-currency bonds.
subfiles.summary: Legible passages concern dollar bonds, repatriated bonds, and requested advice.

subfiles.title: Concurrence routing sheet
subfiles.about: Offices are asked for written concurrence on the attached securities message.
subfiles.summary: The sheet routes the draft for written concurrence.

subfiles.title: Draft telegram on listing Japanese dollar securities
subfiles.about: The draft addresses restoration of bondholder rights before Japanese dollar bonds trade in New York.
subfiles.summary: It seeks reports from obligors, revision of Japan’s 1943 bond law, restoration of mortgage liens, and SCAP recommendations.

subfiles.title: SCAP message on Japanese dollar securities
subfiles.about: SCAP explains wartime conversion of Japanese foreign-currency bonds and current payment constraints.
subfiles.summary: The 1943 law converted municipal and corporate bonds into government obligations and released corporate mortgages; foreign exchange for servicing remains unavailable.

subfiles.title: London airgram on Japanese loan interest
subfiles.about: The embassy reports a House of Commons exchange on overdue Japanese loan interest.
subfiles.summary: Members question why Britain cannot collect Japanese loan interest; Douglas Jay cites continuing American aid to Japan.

subfiles.title: Forwarding note to SCAP
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: A London airgram about Japanese loans is forwarded for SCAP’s information.
subfiles.summary: Forwards a copy of airgram A-2237.

subfiles.title: London airgram on British occupation costs
subfiles.about: The embassy reports a parliamentary answer on Britain’s cost of occupying Japan.
subfiles.summary: The reported total is £10.673 million; the dollar share is described as very small.

subfiles.title: Political Adviser’s despatch transmitting Dodge statement
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards Joseph Dodge’s December 4 press statement.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Dodge’s statement on Japan’s budget and stabilization program.

subfiles.title: Joseph Dodge press conference statement
subfiles.about: Dodge reviews Japan’s stabilized finances and the need for competitive exports.
subfiles.summary: Dodge credits a balanced budget, tax changes, debt reduction, savings, and industrial credit to the stabilization program. He warns that inflationary pressures persist and argues that Japan’s export prospects depend on efficient production, quality, competitive prices, and sound public finances.

subfiles.title: Senator Green’s inquiry about Japanese gold and silver
subfiles.about: Green requests figures for Japan’s gold and silver stocks and possible peace-treaty provisions.
subfiles.summary: He asks for holdings, postwar purchases, and proposed disposition in a peace treaty.

subfiles.title: Reply to Senator Green
subfiles.from: Jack K. McFall, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The Department answers Green’s inquiry about Japanese precious metals.
subfiles.summary: It encloses stock figures, reports no postwar Japanese purchases, and says treaty disposition remains undecided.

subfiles.title: Tabulation of gold and silver stocks in Japan
subfiles.about: A table accounts for gold and silver in custody in Japan.
subfiles.summary: It separates non-Japanese holdings, restitution claims, revolving-fund security, and unencumbered balances.

subfiles.title: Airgram on counterpart fund loans for small businesses
subfiles.about: Tokyo forwards a news release on proposed small-business counterpart fund lending.
subfiles.summary: The proposal would route loans through banks, which would fund 20–30 percent of each loan.

subfiles.title: Airgram on Japanese public employee bonuses
subfiles.about: Tokyo reports a dispute over civil servant and railway worker bonuses.
subfiles.summary: The Cabinet proposes average year-end bonuses of 3,000 yen while unions seek higher payments and wage increases. The report describes budget objections, labor protests, and concerns that unresolved demands could strengthen Communist influence.

subfiles.title: Airgram on two counterpart fund loans
subfiles.about: Tokyo reports approval of loans to chemical and coal producers.
subfiles.summary: Loans totaling 301 million yen support fertilizer chemicals and high-grade coal production.

subfiles.title: Reply to Erleen McConnell about City of Tokyo bonds
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The Department explains its position on private foreign bonds.
subfiles.summary: Corliss directs McConnell to the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council and says peace-settlement treatment is undecided.

subfiles.title: Erleen McConnell’s letter to President Truman
subfiles.about: McConnell asks the President to help secure payment of her Japanese bonds.
subfiles.summary: She says her savings purchased the bonds through a national bank.

subfiles.title: Julia Shine’s inquiry on Tokyo Electric Light bond
subfiles.about: Shine seeks information on a Tokyo Electric Light mortgage gold bond.
subfiles.summary: She identifies a $1,000 bond issued in 1928 and due in 1953.

subfiles.title: Reply to Julia Shine
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The Department responds to Shine’s bond inquiry.
subfiles.summary: The surviving page offers to record bond details and promises public notice of any later government action.

subfiles.title: Reply to Charles Kelly
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The Department answers Kelly’s inquiry about Italian, Japanese, and Bremen bonds.
subfiles.summary: Corliss recommends the bondholders’ council and asks Kelly to supply identifying, purchase, interest, and citizenship details.

subfiles.title: Charles Kelly’s bondholder inquiry
subfiles.about: Kelly asks about interest on Italian, Japanese, and Bremen dollar bonds.
subfiles.summary: He asks for help as a small investor reliant on a pension.

subfiles.title: Financial Affairs memorandum on Posner inquiry
subfiles.about: Financial Affairs asks for a reply to Louis Posner’s bondholder letter.
subfiles.summary: The memo describes the bonds as speculative investments and requests a draft response.

subfiles.title: Legal Adviser note on Posner reply
subfiles.from: W. W. Bishop, Legal Adviser’s Office
subfiles.about: Bishop asks whether Posner should receive the Department’s standard bondholder explanation.
subfiles.summary: A handwritten response says that approach cannot be used.

subfiles.title: Internal memorandum on bondholder inquiries
subfiles.to: Financial Affairs, through the Legal Adviser
subfiles.about: A damaged memorandum discusses the government’s response to bondholders.
subfiles.summary: Legible passages mention the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council and investigation of property status.

subfiles.title: Louis Posner’s inquiry on Tokyo Electric Light bonds
subfiles.to: Special War Problems Division, Department of State
subfiles.about: Posner seeks information on Tokyo Electric Light and its bond trustee.
subfiles.summary: Representing a bondholder, he asks about the company’s and Mitsui Bank’s property and custody under occupation.

subfiles.title: File catch slip
subfiles.about: A records slip requests or reserves a bondholder file paper.
subfiles.summary: The form records a file catch for the November 2 correspondence.

subfiles.title: Army transmittal of Guaranty Trust letters
subfiles.from: Edward F. Witsell, Acting Adjutant General
subfiles.about: The Army forwards two Guaranty Trust letters about Japanese electric utility bonds.
subfiles.summary: Witsell refers the correspondence to State as primarily within its interest.

subfiles.title: Guaranty Trust inquiry on Tokyo Electric Light bonds
subfiles.from: Guaranty Trust Company of New York
subfiles.about: The fiscal agent requests information to answer Tokyo Electric Light bondholders.
subfiles.summary: It reports outstanding bonds and seeks information on war damage, company finances, and the trustee.

subfiles.title: Guaranty Trust inquiry on Toho Electric Power bonds
subfiles.from: Guaranty Trust Company of New York
subfiles.about: The fiscal agent requests information on Toho Electric Power mortgage bonds.
subfiles.summary: It seeks current property and financial information for holders of the outstanding dollar bonds.

subfiles.title: British bondholder’s letter to President Truman
subfiles.about: A British bondholder asks that arrears on Japanese prewar loans be paid.
subfiles.summary: He asks that seized Japanese assets support payment of British bondholders’ interest arrears.

subfiles.title: Instruction to American Mission, London, on Wills letter
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, London
subfiles.about: State suggests how to answer the British bondholder’s appeal.
subfiles.summary: It recommends a British bondholders’ organization and explains that vested Japanese assets await intergovernmental disposition.

subfiles.title: Irving Lindberg’s inquiry on Japanese dollar bonds
subfiles.about: Lindberg asks whether American holders of Japanese dollar bonds are being protected.
subfiles.summary: He asks what steps have been taken on behalf of American investors.

subfiles.title: Instruction to American Mission, Managua
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Managua
subfiles.about: State requests more details before answering Lindberg’s bond inquiry.
subfiles.summary: The mission is asked to obtain the bonds’ identity and acquisition details.

subfiles.title: Copy of Irving Lindberg’s inquiry
subfiles.about: A second copy asks about protection for American holders of Japanese dollar bonds.
subfiles.summary: Lindberg repeats his request for information on investor protection.

subfiles.title: Senate referral to Treasury
subfiles.about: The Senate forwards a constituent’s Japanese bond inquiry to Treasury.
subfiles.summary: It requests consideration and a report with return of the enclosure.

subfiles.title: Treasury reply concerning Senator Mead’s inquiry
subfiles.about: A largely illegible copy concerns a constituent’s Japanese bond inquiry.
subfiles.summary: Only the closing and White’s signature are clearly legible.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Williams and Cocke
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: State acknowledges counsel’s inquiry about Japanese bonds.
subfiles.summary: The Department promises to consider the inquiry and reply later.

subfiles.title: Williams and Cocke inquiry on enemy-country bonds
subfiles.about: Attorneys ask how clients can recover payments on Italian and Japanese bonds.
subfiles.summary: They seek information on government action and steps their clients should take.

subfiles.title: Treasury referral of Mead constituent inquiry
subfiles.from: H. D. White, Assistant Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.about: Treasury forwards Senator Mead’s request about Japanese bond payments.
subfiles.summary: White asks State to consider and answer the enclosed inquiry.

subfiles.title: Frederick Slee’s letter to Senator Mead
subfiles.about: Slee asks when payments on Japanese bonds will resume.
subfiles.summary: He says he represents $13,000 in bonds.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Senator Mead
subfiles.about: State requests identification of the bonds represented by Slee.
subfiles.summary: It asks for obligors, interest rate, issue and maturity dates, and payment currency before further consideration.

subfiles.title: Copy of Frederick Slee’s letter
subfiles.about: A copy repeats Slee’s question about resumed Japanese bond payments.
subfiles.summary: Slee represents $13,000 in bonds.

subfiles.title: Draft or copy of reply to Senator Mead
subfiles.about: A second version asks for details of Slee’s Japanese bonds.
subfiles.summary: It requests bond identification before the Department considers the inquiry further.
